purpose: Contain removed-component writes in plain ECS without a liveness lookup on ordinary writes.

machine.note: Sequential fresh processes, alternating variants. Existing development services left running. No CPU pinning. Snapshot metrics disabled in timing runs.

repeatSelection.reason: Repeat 1 overlapped a heavy unrelated Node workload. Three additional/later repetitions ran after it ended. The host still ran ordinary development services; no CPU pinning or isolation.

source.note: ECS-only production comparison. Both variants use the same harness with an optional live-write phase added to plain ECS churn. Custom registration and docs are outside measured source differences.

method.processes: Fresh sequential Node processes; alternating variant order
method.transport: Counting transport; no sockets or client decoding in timings
method.clock: 1000 + instance.tick to hold engine-control output constant
method.primaryStatistic: Median of per-process statistics from repeats 2, 3 and 4
method.timingScope: stepMs covers Instance.step; preStepMs is game mutation/structural work; totalMs combines matching mutation/index/step ticks

decodedChurnBefore.note: Actual changed churn workload, official Buffer writer/reader, 2 modes × 3 subscribers × 30 ticks × 60 live components

decodedChurnAfter.note: Actual changed churn workload, official Buffer writer/reader, 2 modes × 3 subscribers × 30 ticks × 60 live components

validation.lifecycleRegression: 12 of 14 new cases fail on the old ECS source. All 14 pass after the change, including direct/shared output and prop/group logs.

interpretation: Same performance ballpark, not a claim of zero overhead. Primary idle mean rises 0.037 ms and dense-shared rises 0.049 ms; sparse-shared is nearly unchanged and churn with writes improves slightly. Individual repeats and the unchanged spatial control vary, so these numbers do not establish a precise causal cost.
